reader_summary.headline: DNOW could double by 2029 despite past struggles and recent mergers.
reader_summary.overview: The episode argues that DNOW is a resilient distributor that grew margins even while the oil industry struggled. A recent merger adds significant savings, and management targets strong future cash flow. The host also discusses risks like high debt and weak governance, while sharing lessons on why selling winning stocks is difficult.

key_points.text: DNOW spun out of National Oilwell Varco at $35 in late 2014. A year later it was $13. Today it is around $16.
key_points.evidence_quote: DNOW spun out of National Oilwell Varco at $35 in late 2014. A year later it was $13. Today it is around $16.

key_points.text: The MRC Global merger brings $75m of synergies to two businesses that earned $325m of EBITDA apart in 2024.
key_points.evidence_quote: The MRC Global merger brings $75m of synergies to two businesses that earned $325m of EBITDA apart in 2024.

key_points.text: Management has soft-targeted $350m of EBITDA for 2027 against roughly a $3.5B enterprise value.
key_points.evidence_quote: Management has soft-targeted $350m of EBITDA for 2027 against roughly a $3.5B enterprise value, which Steve gets to about $300m of free cash flow on a $3B market cap.

key_points.text: The governance knock: a company named after a sub-1% CEO.
